title: Transfer a vehicle registration due to the death of the registered operator
summary: You can transfer a vehicle registration into your name at a Service NSW Centre if the original owner has died.
intro:
If you need to transfer a vehicle registration into your name because the vehicle owner has died, you can do this at a Service NSW Centre.

The registration may be transferred into the name of one of the following:
who_can_apply: The vehicle owner must have died.
The transfer must be done at a Service NSW Centre.
what_you_need: A completed Application for Transfer of Registration – PDF
The original or certified copy of the will, probate, or letters of administration (if transferring to the executor or administrator)
Signed, written advice from a solicitor or NSW Trustee & Guardian (if the will, probate, or letters of administration are unavailable)
The relationship with the deceased (e.g., spouse, sibling, child)
Confirmation that to your knowledge there is no administrator for the estate or no will (if applicable)
Proof of Registration Entitlement (if transferring to a buyer)
Signed advice from the administrator or executor confirming the name of the beneficiary (if transferring to a beneficiary)

how_to_steps.text: Visit a service centre and submit your application.

more_info.text: If the vehicle is disposed of or sold without being transferred to a person named in a will or other acceptable document, the new operator must meet the normal requirements to transfer the registration.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay fees when transferring the registration?
faqs.a: No transfer fee or stamp duty is required when transferring to the executor, administrator, or next of kin. However, if you are transferring to a buyer, you must pay a transfer fee and stamp duty.

faqs.q: What documents are needed if I am transferring to the executor or administrator?
faqs.a: You must provide the original or certified copy of the will, probate, or letters of administration. If these are unavailable, you need signed, written advice from a solicitor or NSW Trustee & Guardian.

faqs.q: What documents are needed if I am transferring to the next of kin?
faqs.a: The next of kin must complete a Statutory Declaration. If the next of kin is under 18, the guardian must complete the declaration.
